records.source: Τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ῥητῶς λέγει ὅτι ἐν ὑστέροις καιροῖς ἀποστήσονταί τινες τῆς πίστεως, προσέχοντες πνεύμασι πλάνοις καὶ διδασκαλίαις δαιμονίων ἐν ὑποκρίσει ψευδολόγων, κεκαυστηριασμένων τὴν ἰδίαν συνείδησιν, κωλυόντων γαμεῖν, ἀπέχεσθαι βρωμάτων ἃ ὁ θεὸς ἔκτισεν εἰς μετάλημψιν μετὰ εὐχαριστίας τοῖς πιστοῖς καὶ ἐπεγνωκόσι τὴν ἀλήθειαν.
records.gloss: The but Spirit expressly says that in later times will depart some from the faith, paying attention to spirits deceitful and teachings of demons, \v 2 in hypocrisy of liars, having been seared [in] their own conscience, \v 3 forbidding to marry, [commanding] to abstain from foods, which the God created for receiving with thanksgiving by the faithful and those having known the truth.
pieces: The Spirit says clearly that in later times some will abandon the faith and follow deceiving spirits and things taught by demons.
Such teaching comes through hypocritical liars whose consciences have been branded as with a hot iron.
They forbid people to marry and order them to keep away from certain foods, which God created to be received with thanks by those who believe and know the truth.

L.1: But the Spirit says explicitly that in later times some will depart from the faith, paying attention to deceitful spirits and teachings of demons,
L.2: through the hypocrisy of liars whose consciences have been seared,
L.3: who forbid marriage [and command people] to abstain from foods, which God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.

R.1: The Spirit clearly tells us that in the last times some people will turn away from the faith. They will listen to spirits who lie, and to things that demons teach.
R.2: These teachings come from people who lie and pretend to be good. Their consciences no longer work, as if they had been burned with a hot iron.
R.3: They say that people must not marry, and they tell them not to eat certain foods. But God made these foods to be eaten with thanks by people who believe and know the truth.

decisions.choice: the Spirit says explicitly: through prophecy in the church
decisions.reason: ῥητῶς means clearly, in so many words. The Spirit's warning may have come through prophets in the church (4:14) or through teachings like Mark 13:22 and Acts 20:29-30.

decisions.choice: in later times: the time already beginning
decisions.reason: The teachers Timothy faces are evidence that these times have begun (2 Timothy 3:1-5).

decisions.choice: consciences seared: branded, or made insensible
decisions.reason: καυστηριάζω is to brand with a hot iron, as slaves and criminals were marked, or to cauterize so that the flesh feels nothing. Either way their conscience no longer warns them.

decisions.choice: forbidding marriage and foods: a teaching that made holiness depend on denying the body
decisions.reason: Some teachers in Ephesus held that marriage and certain foods were unspiritual (compare Colossians 2:20-23). The letter answers from creation: what God made is good (verse 4).

decisions.choice: the faithful: believers
decisions.reason: πιστοῖς here means those who believe, parallel to "those who know the truth".

decisions.choice: branded as with a hot iron (B); as if they had been burned with a hot iron (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the picture (m3).

records.heading: Some will abandon the faith

records.source: ὅτι πᾶν κτίσμα θεοῦ καλόν, καὶ οὐδὲν ἀπόβλητον μετὰ εὐχαριστίας λαμβανόμενον, ἁγιάζεται γὰρ διὰ λόγου θεοῦ καὶ ἐντεύξεως.
records.gloss: because every creature of God [is] good, and nothing to be rejected with thanksgiving being received, \v 5 it is sanctified for through [the] word of God and prayer.
pieces: For everything God created is good, and nothing should be refused if it is received with thanks,
because it is made holy by God's word and by prayer.

L.4: For everything created by God [is] good, and nothing is to be rejected if it is received with thanksgiving,
L.5: for it is made holy by [the] word of God and prayer.

R.4: Everything that God made is good. We should not refuse any food if we thank God for it.
R.5: It is made holy by what God has said and by our prayers.

decisions.choice: everything created by God is good: Genesis 1:31
decisions.reason: "God saw everything that he had made, and indeed, it was very good" (Genesis 1:31).

decisions.choice: made holy by the word of God and prayer: God's word declaring it good, and the prayer of thanks at meals
decisions.reason: "The word of God" may be the creation word of Genesis or the words of Scripture used in giving thanks; "prayer" is the thanksgiving said over food.

decisions.choice: We should not refuse any food if we thank God for it
alternatives: nothing is to be rejected if it is received with thanksgiving
decisions.reason: Readable names what is in view: food (verse 3).

records.source: Ταῦτα ὑποτιθέμενος τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς καλὸς ἔσῃ διάκονος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ἐντρεφόμενος τοῖς λόγοις τῆς πίστεως καὶ τῆς καλῆς διδασκαλίας ᾗ παρηκολούθηκας, τοὺς δὲ βεβήλους καὶ γραώδεις μύθους παραιτοῦ.
records.gloss: These things pointing out to the brothers a good you will be servant of Christ Jesus, being nourished in the words of the faith and of the good teaching which you have followed; \v 7 the but profane and old-womanish myths refuse.
pieces: If you teach these things to the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you will be a good servant of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, feeding yourself on the words of the faith and of the good teaching you have followed.
Have nothing to do with godless and silly myths.

L.6: If you point these things out to the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you will be a good servant of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, nourished in the words of the faith and of the good teaching that you have followed.
L.7: But refuse profane myths fit only for old women.

R.6: If you teach these things to the believers, you will be a good servant of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. Keep feeding your own soul with the words of the faith and the good teaching that you have followed.
R.7: Do not pay any attention to silly stories that have nothing to do with God.

decisions.choice: servant: one who serves Christ
decisions.reason: διάκονος here has its general sense of servant, as in Colossians 1:7.

decisions.choice: nourished in the words of the faith: fed by sound teaching
decisions.reason: ἐντρέφομαι is to be brought up on, nourished by: Timothy has grown up on sound teaching (2 Timothy 3:14-15).

decisions.choice: myths fit for old women: a dismissive expression, "old wives' tales"
decisions.reason: γραώδεις was a common insult for foolish, idle tales; it dismisses the stories, not women. βεβήλους means profane, without holiness.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: silly
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m3); Literal keeps its form.

records.heading: Train yourself in godliness

R.7: Instead, work hard to train yourself to live in a way that pleases God.

decisions.choice: train: as an athlete trains
decisions.reason: γυμνάζω is the word for athletic training, the root of "gymnasium". Verse 8 develops the picture.

decisions.choice: to live in a way that pleases God
decisions.reason: Readable explains "godliness" (2:2).

records.source: ἡ γὰρ σωματικὴ γυμνασία πρὸς ὀλίγον ἐστὶν ὠφέλιμος, ἡ δὲ εὐσέβεια πρὸς πάντα ὠφέλιμός ἐστιν, ἐπαγγελίαν ἔχουσα ζωῆς τῆς νῦν καὶ τῆς μελλούσης.
records.gloss: the for bodily training for little is profitable, the but godliness for all things profitable is, promise having of life the now and the coming.
pieces: Physical training has some value, but godliness is valuable in every way, since it holds promise both for life now and for the life to come.

L.8: For bodily training is of some value, but godliness is valuable for everything, holding promise for the present life and for the life to come.

R.8: Exercising your body helps you a little. But living to please God helps you in every way. It brings blessings in this life and in the life that is coming.

decisions.choice: bodily training of little value: some value, but limited
decisions.reason: πρὸς ὀλίγον can mean "for a little while" or "for a little": bodily training has real but limited worth. It may glance at the false teachers' severe treatment of the body (verse 3).

decisions.choice: the present life and the life to come
decisions.reason: Godliness brings what God promises both now and in the age to come (Mark 10:29-30).

records.source: πιστὸς ὁ λόγος καὶ πάσης ἀποδοχῆς ἄξιος, εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ κοπιῶμεν καὶ ὀνειδιζόμεθα, ὅτι ἠλπίκαμεν ἐπὶ θεῷ ζῶντι, ὅς ἐστιν σωτὴρ πάντων ἀνθρώπων, μάλιστα πιστῶν.
records.gloss: Trustworthy [is] the saying and of all acceptance worthy; \v 10 for this for we labor and suffer reproach, because we have hoped on God living, who is Savior of all men, especially of believers.
pieces: Here is a saying you can rely on, which deserves to be fully accepted.
This is why we work hard and endure insults: we have put our hope in the living God, the Savior of {{gender:all people|all men}}, and especially of those who believe.

L.9: The saying [is] trustworthy and worthy of full acceptance.
L.10: For to this end we labor and suffer reproach, because we have set our hope on [the] living God, who is [the] Savior of {{gender:all people|all men}}, especially of believers.

R.9: Here is something true that everyone should accept.
R.10: That is why we work so hard and why people insult us. We have put our hope in the living God. He is the Savior of all people, and most of all of those who believe.

decisions.choice: the saying: the words of verse 8 or verse 10
decisions.reason: The formula may point back to verse 8 or ahead to verse 10; the SBLGNT punctuation leaves it standing between them.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "suffer reproach"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "we strive", a verb that looks similar in Greek. The SBLGNT reads ὀνειδιζόμεθα.

decisions.choice: the Savior of all people, especially of believers
alternatives: "especially" meaning "that is": the Savior of all, namely of believers
decisions.reason: God is the Savior of all people in that he cares for all and offers salvation to all (2:4); he saves in the full sense those who believe. μάλιστα usually means "especially"; some take it as "that is". The verse does not say that all will in fact be saved.

decisions.choice: {{gender:all people|all men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general; "men" is the traditional form.

pieces: Give these instructions, and teach them.

R.11: Tell people to do these things, and teach them.

decisions.choice: command: give orders with authority
decisions.reason: παραγγέλλω is the word of 1:3: Timothy is to speak with authority.

records.heading: Set the believers an example

records.source: μηδείς σου τῆς νεότητος καταφρονείτω, ἀλλὰ τύπος γίνου τῶν πιστῶν ἐν λόγῳ, ἐν ἀναστροφῇ, ἐν ἀγάπῃ, ἐν πίστει, ἐν ἁγνείᾳ.
records.gloss: No one your youth let despise, but an example be for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
pieces: Do not let anyone look down on you because you are young, but set the believers an example in how you speak and live, in love, in faith and in purity.

L.12: Let no one look down on your youth, but be an example to the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.

R.12: Do not let anyone think you are not important because you are young. Show the believers how to live by the way you speak and act, and by your love, your faith and your pure life.

decisions.choice: youth: relative youth, for a leader
decisions.reason: νεότητος could describe anyone up to about forty in that culture. Timothy had worked with Paul for many years (Acts 16:1-3), but was young for a leader of older men.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "in love, in faith, in purity"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "in spirit" after "in love".

records.source: ἕως ἔρχομαι πρόσεχε τῇ ἀναγνώσει, τῇ παρακλήσει, τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ.
records.gloss: Until I come, give attention to the reading, to the exhortation, to the teaching.
pieces: Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to preaching and to teaching.

L.13: Until I come, give attention to the [public] reading, to exhortation, to teaching.

R.13: Until I come, keep reading the Scriptures aloud to the church. Encourage the people, and teach them.

decisions.choice: the reading, exhortation and teaching of the gathered church
decisions.reason: ἀναγνώσει is the public reading of Scripture in the assembly, as in the synagogue (Luke 4:16-20; Acts 13:15). παρακλήσει is the appeal or sermon based on it, διδασκαλίᾳ instruction.

decisions.choice: the public reading of Scripture (B); reading the Scriptures aloud to the church (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what is read and where (m1).

records.source: μὴ ἀμέλει τοῦ ἐν σοὶ χαρίσματος, ὃ ἐδόθη σοι διὰ προφητείας μετὰ ἐπιθέσεως τῶν χειρῶν τοῦ πρεσβυτερίου.
records.gloss: Not neglect the in you gift, which was given to you through prophecy with [the] laying on of the hands of the council of elders.
pieces: Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given to you through a prophetic word when the elders laid their hands on you.

L.14: Do not neglect the gift in you, which was given to you through prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the council of elders.

R.14: God has given you a gift. Do not forget to use it. You received it when the church leaders put their hands on you and God gave a message through prophecy.

decisions.choice: gift: a gift of God's grace for service
decisions.reason: χαρίσματος is a gift of grace (Romans 12:6), here the gift Timothy received for his work.

decisions.choice: the laying on of hands by the council of elders
decisions.reason: Laying hands on someone was a sign of setting them apart for a task (Numbers 27:18-23; Acts 6:6; 13:3). In 2 Timothy 1:6 Paul speaks of his own hands; he and the elders may have acted together. πρεσβυτερίου is the body of elders.

decisions.choice: through prophecy: with a prophetic word spoken at the time
decisions.reason: Compare 1:18: prophetic words accompanied Timothy's commissioning.

records.source: ταῦτα μελέτα, ἐν τούτοις ἴσθι, ἵνα σου ἡ προκοπὴ φανερὰ ᾖ πᾶσιν·
records.gloss: These things practice, in these be, so that your progress evident may be to all;
pieces: Put these things into practice and give yourself wholly to them, so that everyone may see your progress.

L.15: Practice these things, be absorbed in them, so that your progress may be evident to all.

R.15: Work hard at these things, and give yourself to them completely. Then everyone will see how you are growing.

decisions.choice: practice, be in them
decisions.reason: μελετάω means to practice or to give careful thought to; "be in them" means be wholly occupied with them.

records.source: ἔπεχε σεαυτῷ καὶ τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ· ἐπίμενε αὐτοῖς· τοῦτο γὰρ ποιῶν καὶ σεαυτὸν σώσεις καὶ τοὺς ἀκούοντάς σου.
records.gloss: Pay attention to yourself and to the teaching; persist in them; this for doing both yourself you will save and those hearing you.
pieces: Keep a close watch on yourself and on your teaching. Persevere in them, for if you do, you will save both yourself and your hearers.

L.16: Pay close attention to yourself and to the teaching. Persist in these things, for by doing this you will save both yourself and those who hear you.

R.16: Be careful about how you live and what you teach. Keep doing these things. If you do, God will save you and the people who listen to you.

decisions.choice: you will save both yourself and your hearers: through faithful life and teaching God saves
decisions.reason: σῴζω is to save. Timothy does not save by his own power; faithful teaching is the means by which God brings salvation to teacher and hearers (1 Corinthians 9:22; James 5:20).

decisions.choice: God will save you
decisions.reason: Readable says who saves (m1).
